instruction: Fill in the Thunderbird account setup with name 'Test Account' and email address 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com'.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Thunderbird, navigated to Account Setup form, filled name as 'Anonym User', email as 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com', and password. Stayed on setup page but never clicked Continue, so IMAP was never shown. Evaluator expected 'Anonym Tester' not 'Anonym User'.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can interact with Thunderbird UI, click form fields, clear and type text, fill name/email/password fields, switch between windows
metadata.failure_analysis: Model typed 'Anonym User' instead of expected 'Anonym Tester' for the name. Also never clicked Continue so IMAP protocol info was not displayed. The 4-xpath evaluator required all conditions including IMAP visibility.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed to two-step: fill name and email fields. Model demonstrated ability to fill both fields successfully in the trajectory. Partial credit if only one field is correct.
metadata.explanation: Task requires filling name and email in Thunderbird account setup. Evaluator checks accessibility tree for both 'Test Account' name and email address. Each xpath gives 0.5 partial credit.

scoring_breakdown.name_filled: 0.5 - Display name 'Test Account' present in accessibility tree

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_accessibility_tree) correctly retrieves UI state needed to verify form field values in Thunderbird.
Metric (check_accessibility_tree) correctly receives the rules list and iterates over xpath rules to check element presence.
Both instruction requirements are covered: name 'Test Account' and email 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com' are each verified by separate xpath rules.
XPath expressions use contains(text(), ...) or contains(@name, ...) which appropriately matches form field values in the accessibility tree.

Minor inaccuracy: metadata claims 'Each xpath gives 0.5 partial credit' but check_accessibility_tree returns 0.0 immediately if any rule finds no matching elements (line 253), so there is no actual partial credit. Evaluation is all-or-nothing.
Postconfig with 1-second sleep is reasonable for UI stabilization before reading the accessibility tree.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: If partial credit is desired, consider using a different metric or custom function that scores each rule independently (e.g., 0.5 per matched rule) rather than returning 0.0 on first failure.
Update metadata scoring_breakdown to accurately reflect the all-or-nothing scoring behavior of check_accessibility_tree.
